title: Current architecture beats conflicting repository behavior

input.prompt: The repository puts sync state inside the renderer, but the current architecture says the data runtime owns sync state. Which source should drive the fix?
context: Architecture document is explicitly Current Authority.
Repository behavior is deployed but undocumented as a design decision.

required_findings: Repository behavior does not override current architecture authority.
This is implementation or architecture drift unless a new authority change is accepted.
forbidden_findings: Promote the repository structure to architecture authority because it already exists.

title: Two current authorities that disagree block downstream work

input.prompt: Spec A and Spec B are both marked Current Authority and disagree on operation ordering. Can we continue implementation?

required_findings: One effective authority must be established before downstream work continues.
forbidden_findings: Pick the newer file automatically without supersession evidence.

title: Newer draft does not supersede older current authority

input.prompt: A draft v0.3 was edited yesterday, while v0.2 is still marked Current Authority. Which one should implementation follow?

required_findings: Freshness does not make a draft current authority.
forbidden_findings: Use v0.3 because it was modified more recently.

input.prompt: An old RFC says batching is canonical, but its header says Superseded by the current operation-only model. Which rule is effective?

required_findings: The superseded RFC can explain history but cannot compete with current authority.
forbidden_findings: Treat both documents as equally authoritative.

title: Historical ADR cannot override current baseline

input.prompt: A historical ADR chose a native data runtime, but the current baseline says TS-first. The old ADR is more detailed. Which should we implement?
context: Current baseline explicitly supersedes the old direction.

required_findings: Detail level does not outrank current authority status.
forbidden_findings: Prefer the old ADR because it contains more implementation detail.

title: Stale tests are evidence drift, not authority

input.prompt: The current semantic spec changed a field default, but old golden tests still enforce the previous default. The implementation matches the new spec and tests fail.
context: The spec change was accepted and supersession is complete.

required_findings: Tests must be updated to prove the current contract, not the superseded behavior.
forbidden_findings: Revert the implementation to make stale tests pass.

title: Missing contract discovered during implementation blocks downstream work

input.prompt: While implementing reconnect, we discovered that ordering across local and remote replay is not defined anywhere. Can Codex choose a reasonable ordering?
context: The missing rule affects observable canonical state.

required_findings: Codex must not invent canonical ordering semantics in implementation.
forbidden_findings: Choose the simplest ordering and document it afterward.

title: Accepted new authority with stale master index requires supersession closure

input.prompt: Architecture v0.4 is accepted and marked Current, but the master index and implementation plan still point to v0.3. What is the correct next step?
context: Downstream tasks have not been rebased.

required_findings: Update master/index and downstream version dependencies before resuming implementation.
forbidden_findings: Continue because the new architecture document itself is already current.
